import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Categoricity of atomic models

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Categorical theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace Categorical

open Cardinal FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

/-- A complete type is isolated if some formula belongs to it and to no other complete type. -/
def IsIsolatedType {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {T : L.Theory} {α : Type w}
    (p : T.CompleteType α) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ : L[[α]].Sentence, FirstOrder.Language.Theory.CompleteType.typesWith φ = {p}

/-- A model is atomic if the complete type of each of its finite tuples is isolated. -/
def IsAtomicModel {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {T : L.Theory}
    (M : FirstOrder.Language.Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → M), IsIsolatedType (T.typeOf a)

/--
The class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ` if an atomic model of cardinality `κ`
exists and any two atomic models of cardinality `κ` are isomorphic.
-/
def IsAtomicCategorical {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (κ : Cardinal.{w})
    (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : FirstOrder.Language.Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T,
      IsAtomicModel M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : FirstOrder.Language.Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T,
      IsAtomicModel M → IsAtomicModel N → #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/--
**Shelah's categoricity problem for atomic models.** If the class of atomic models of a complete
first-order theory in a countable language is categorical in every cardinal $\aleph_n$ for
$n < \omega$, is it categorical in every infinite cardinal? Here categoricity includes the
existence of an atomic model of the specified cardinality, as well as uniqueness up to isomorphism.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem categorical :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} [Countable L.Symbols] {T : L.Theory}, T.IsComplete →
        (∀ n : ℕ, IsAtomicCategorical (Cardinal.aleph n) T) →
          ∀ κ : Cardinal.{w}, ℵ₀ ≤ κ → IsAtomicCategorical κ T := by
  sorry

end Categorical
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “the ℵ_n” as every `Cardinal.aleph n` for `n : ℕ`, following the fixed decomposition.
Made the implicit countable-language hypothesis explicit as `[Countable L.Symbols]`.
Interpreted “every cardinal” as every infinite cardinal, encoded by `ℵ₀ ≤ κ`.

Defined categoricity of the atomic class to include existence of an atomic model of the specified cardinality as well as pairwise isomorphism of all atomic models of that cardinality; Mathlib's existing `Cardinal.Categorical` only gives the latter.
Encoded an atomic model by requiring every finite tuple, indexed by `Fin n`, to realize an isolated complete type over the theory.
Used a universe-polymorphic statement; within each instantiation, cardinals and model carriers lie in the same universe.

/-!
# Categoricity of atomic models

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Categorical theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace Categorical

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

universe u v w

/-- A complete type is isolated if some formula in it belongs to no other complete type. -/
def IsIsolatedType {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {T : L.Theory} {α : Type w}
    (p : T.CompleteType α) : Prop :=
  ∃ φ ∈ p, ∀ q : T.CompleteType α, φ ∈ q → q = p

/-- A model is atomic if the type over the empty set of every finite tuple is isolated. -/
def IsAtomicModel {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {T : L.Theory}
    (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) : Prop :=
  ∀ n (a : Fin n → M), IsIsolatedType (T.typeOf a)

/-- The atomic models of `T` are categorical in `κ` if one of size `κ` exists and any two
atomic models of size `κ` are isomorphic. -/
def AtomicCategorical {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (κ : Cardinal.{w})
    (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel M ∧ Cardinal.mk M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel M → IsAtomicModel N →
      Cardinal.mk M = κ → Cardinal.mk N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/--
If the class of atomic models of a complete first-order theory in a countable language is
categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every $n < \omega$, is it categorical in every infinite cardinal?
Categoricity here includes the existence of an atomic model of the specified cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem categorical :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) (_ : Countable L.Symbols) (T : L.Theory), T.IsComplete →
        (∀ n : ℕ, AtomicCategorical (Cardinal.aleph n) T) →
          ∀ κ : Cardinal.{w}, Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ κ → AtomicCategorical κ T := by
  sorry

end Categorical
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “the aleph_n” as every `Cardinal.aleph n` for `n : ℕ`, as specified by the decomposition.
Encoded the implicit countable-language assumption as `Countable L.Symbols`, matching the existing Vaught conjecture formalization.
Used Mathlib's `Theory.IsComplete`, which includes satisfiability as well as semantic completeness.
Defined a complete type to be isolated when it contains a formula that belongs to no other complete type; this is the standard singleton-basic-open characterization of an isolated (principal) type.
Defined an atomic model by requiring the complete type over the empty set of every tuple indexed by `Fin n`, for every `n : ℕ`, to be isolated.

Defined categoricity for atomic models to require both existence of an atomic model of the specified cardinality and pairwise isomorphism of all such models, because existence is not automatic for this non-elementary class.
Interpreted “every cardinal” as every infinite cardinal (`Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ κ`) in the model universe. The conclusion therefore includes the countable cardinal, as requested by the decomposition.
Scoped `answer(sorry)` over the full universal implication, so a positive answer asserts the stated transfer for every complete theory in a countable language.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Categoricity of the class of atomic models

Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory in a countable language. A model $M$ of $T$ is *atomic*
if every finite tuple $\bar a$ of elements of $M$ realizes an isolated (principal) type over $T$,
that is, there is a formula $\varphi(\bar x)$ true of $\bar a$ such that every formula
$\psi(\bar x)$ true of $\bar a$ satisfies $T \models \forall \bar x\,(\varphi(\bar x) \to
\psi(\bar x))$.

The class $K$ of atomic models of $T$ is *categorical in $\lambda$* if $K$ has exactly one model
of cardinality $\lambda$ up to isomorphism. Since $K$ is not an elementary class, the
Löwenheim–Skolem theorem does not provide models of every infinite cardinality for free, so
existence of a model of cardinality $\lambda$ is part of the definition.

Shelah proved that if $2^{\aleph_n} < 2^{\aleph_{n+1}}$ for every $n < \omega$ and $K$ is
categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every $n < \omega$, then $K$ is categorical in every infinite
cardinal. Whether the set-theoretic hypothesis can be removed is open:

*If the class of atomic models of a complete first order theory is categorical in the
$\aleph_n$, is it categorical in every cardinal?*

*References:*
- [Wikipedia: Categorical theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia: List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- S. Shelah, *Classification theory for nonelementary classes, I. The number of uncountable
  models of $\psi \in L_{\omega_1,\omega}$. Parts A, B*, Israel J. Math. 46 (1983), 212–240 and
  241–273.
- J. T. Baldwin, *Categoricity*, University Lecture Series 50, AMS (2009).
-/

universe u v w

open Cardinal FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

namespace Categorical

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {T : L.Theory}

/-- A model `M` of `T` is *atomic* if every finite tuple `v` of elements of `M` realizes an
isolated type over `T`: there is a formula `φ` true of `v` such that every formula `ψ` true of
`v` is implied by `φ` modulo `T`, i.e. `T ⊨ ∀ x̄, φ x̄ → ψ x̄`. -/
def IsAtomic (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → M), ∃ φ : L.Formula (Fin n),
    φ.Realize v ∧ ∀ ψ : L.Formula (Fin n), ψ.Realize v → T ⊨ᵇ φ ⟹ ψ

/-- The class of atomic models of `T` is *categorical in `κ`* if it has exactly one model of
cardinality `κ` up to isomorphism: there is an atomic model of `T` of cardinality `κ`, and any two
atomic models of `T` of cardinality `κ` are isomorphic. -/
def AtomicCategorical (κ : Cardinal.{w}) (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : T.ModelType, IsAtomic M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : T.ModelType, IsAtomic M → IsAtomic N → #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/-- Being atomic is invariant under isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem IsAtomic.of_equiv {M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T} (f : M ≃[L] N) (hM : IsAtomic M) :
    IsAtomic N := by
  intro n v
  obtain ⟨φ, hφ, h⟩ := hM n (f.symm ∘ v)
  have hv : f ∘ (f.symm ∘ v) = v := by ext; simp
  refine ⟨φ, ?_, fun ψ hψ => h ψ ?_⟩
  · rwa [← hv, StrongHomClass.realize_formula]
  · rwa [← hv, StrongHomClass.realize_formula] at hψ

/-- If `T` is `κ`-categorical and has an atomic model of cardinality `κ`, then the class of
atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem atomicCategorical_of_categorical {κ : Cardinal.{w}} (h : κ.Categorical T)
    (hM : ∃ M : T.ModelType, IsAtomic M ∧ #M = κ) : AtomicCategorical κ T :=
  ⟨hM, fun M N _ _ hM hN => h M N hM hN⟩

/-- If the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`, then `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem AtomicCategorical.exists_isAtomic {κ : Cardinal.{w}} (h : AtomicCategorical κ T) :
    ∃ M : T.ModelType, IsAtomic M ∧ #M = κ :=
  h.1

/-- **Shelah's categoricity problem for atomic classes.** Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory
in a countable language. If the class of atomic models of $T$ is categorical in $\aleph_n$ for
every $n < \omega$, is it categorical in every infinite cardinal?

Here "categorical in $\lambda$" means that there is exactly one atomic model of $T$ of
cardinality $\lambda$ up to isomorphism (existence included). Shelah proved the answer is yes
under the assumption $2^{\aleph_n} < 2^{\aleph_{n+1}}$ for all $n < \omega$; the question is
whether this holds in ZFC alone. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem categorical :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) (T : L.Theory), Countable L.Symbols →
      T.IsComplete → (∀ n : ℕ, AtomicCategorical.{u, v, w} (ℵ_ n) T) →
        ∀ κ : Cardinal.{w}, ℵ₀ ≤ κ → AtomicCategorical κ T := by
  sorry

end Categorical
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (countable language, all ℵ_n, existence included in categoricity, every infinite cardinal, yes/no via answer(sorry)) match the source and Shelah's problem as stated in Sh87a/b and Baldwin's 'Categoricity'.
modeling_decisions: 'Complete first order theory' is taken in a countable language (implicit in Shelah's problem and stated in the decomposition notes); formalized as `Countable L.Symbols` following the existing `VaughtConjecture.lean` idiom. `T.IsComplete` in Mathlib includes satisfiability.

'Categorical in the ℵ_n' is read as categorical in ℵ_n for every n < ω, formalized as `∀ n : ℕ, AtomicCategorical (ℵ_ n) T` (Mathlib's `aleph` is indexed so that `ℵ_ 0 = ℵ₀`). Including n = 0 (ℵ₀) is harmless: the countable atomic model, if it exists, is unique, and the conclusion also covers ℵ₀.

'Categorical in λ' includes existence of an atomic model of cardinality λ (`AtomicCategorical κ T := (∃ atomic M with #M = κ) ∧ (any two atomic models of size κ are isomorphic)`). Mathlib's `Cardinal.Categorical` only asserts uniqueness; since the class of atomic models is not elementary, Löwenheim–Skolem does not give existence, and Shelah/Baldwin's definition ('K has exactly one model of power λ') includes existence. Without existence, a theory with no atomic models at all would be trivially categorical everywhere.

'Every cardinal' is read as every infinite cardinal (`∀ κ, ℵ₀ ≤ κ → …`). If T (complete) has an infinite model it has no finite models, so with the existence requirement categoricity in a finite cardinal is impossible whenever the hypothesis holds; finite κ therefore cannot be intended.

Atomic model: `IsAtomic M` says every tuple `v : Fin n → M` (all n, including n = 0, which is harmless for complete T) satisfies some formula φ such that every formula ψ true of v satisfies `T ⊨ᵇ φ ⟹ ψ`, i.e. T ⊨ ∀x̄ (φ → ψ). This is the standard 'every tuple realizes an isolated (principal) type over T' definition; for a model of a complete theory it coincides with isolation over Th(M).

Isolation is defined syntactically (via `T ⊨ᵇ`) rather than topologically via Mathlib's `CompleteType`/`typesWith`; the two are equivalent by compactness, and the syntactic form matches the textbook definition directly.

Universes: L : Language.{u, v}; the atomic models quantified over in both hypothesis and conclusion live in `Type w` (κ : Cardinal.{w}), matching Mathlib's `Cardinal.Categorical`. Since categoricity is about isomorphism types of models of cardinality κ, and every such structure has an isomorphic copy in `Type w`, this is faithful. `T ⊨ᵇ` in `IsAtomic` quantifies over models in `Type (max u v)`, as in Mathlib.
The theorem is universe-polymorphic in u v w (a family of statements); with the `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ …` form there are no explicit binders, as required by the repository's answer linter.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Categoricity of the class of atomic models of a complete theory

Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory in a countable language. A model $M$ of $T$ is
*atomic* if every finite tuple of elements of $M$ realizes a complete type that is isolated
(principal) over $T$. The class of atomic models of $T$ is not an elementary class, so
Morley's categoricity theorem does not apply to it.

Shelah asked: if the class of atomic models of $T$ is categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every
$n < \omega$, is it categorical in every infinite cardinal? Shelah proved that the answer is
positive under the set-theoretic hypothesis $2^{\aleph_n} < 2^{\aleph_{n+1}}$ for all $n < \omega$.
Whether the answer is positive in ZFC alone is open.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Categorical (model theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- S. Shelah, *Classification theory for nonelementary classes, I. The number of uncountable
  models of $\psi \in L_{\omega_1,\omega}$. Parts A and B*, Israel J. Math. 46 (1983), 212–273.
- J. T. Baldwin, *Categoricity*, University Lecture Series 50, AMS, 2009.
-/

namespace Categorical

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Cardinal

universe u v w

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory)

/-- A model `M` of `T` is *atomic* if every finite tuple `v` of elements of `M` realizes a
complete type that is isolated over `T`. That is, there is a formula `φ` satisfied by `v` such
that `T ⊨ ∀ x, (φ x → ψ x)` for every formula `ψ` satisfied by `v`. -/
def IsAtomicModel (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → M), ∃ φ : L.Formula (Fin n), φ.Realize v ∧
    ∀ ψ : L.Formula (Fin n), ψ.Realize v → T ⊨ᵇ φ.imp ψ

/-- The class of atomic models of `T` is *categorical in `κ`* if it contains exactly one model
of cardinality `κ` up to isomorphism: there is an atomic model of `T` of cardinality `κ`, and any
two atomic models of `T` of cardinality `κ` are isomorphic. Existence is part of the definition
because the class of atomic models is not an elementary class, so the Löwenheim–Skolem theorem
does not provide atomic models of every infinite cardinality. -/
def IsAtomicCategorical (κ : Cardinal.{w}) : Prop :=
  ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ ∧
    ∀ N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T N → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/-- If the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`, then `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem IsAtomicCategorical.exists_isAtomicModel {κ : Cardinal.{w}}
    (h : IsAtomicCategorical T κ) :
    ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ := by
  obtain ⟨M, hM, hκ, -⟩ := h
  exact ⟨M, hM, hκ⟩

/-- If `T` is `κ`-categorical and has an atomic model of cardinality `κ`, then the class of atomic
models of `T` is categorical in `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]

/-!
# Categoricity of the class of atomic models of a complete theory

Shelah's problem on the categoricity spectrum of atomic classes: if the class of atomic models
of a complete first order theory (in a countable language) is categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every
$n < \omega$, is it categorical in every infinite cardinal?

Shelah proved a positive answer under the set-theoretic hypothesis
$2^{\aleph_n} < 2^{\aleph_{n+1}}$ for all $n < \omega$. The question is open in ZFC.

*References:*

- [Wikipedia, Categorical (model theory)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- S. Shelah, *Classification theory for nonelementary classes. I. The number of uncountable
  models of $\psi \in L_{\omega_1,\omega}$. Parts A and B*, Israel J. Math. 46 (1983).
- J. T. Baldwin, *Categoricity*, AMS University Lecture Series 50 (2009).
-/

namespace Categorical

open Cardinal FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

universe u v w

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} {T : L.Theory}

/-- A model `M` of a theory `T` is *atomic* if every finite tuple `v` of elements of `M` realizes
a principal (isolated) complete type over `T`: there is a formula `φ` satisfied by `v` such that
`T ⊨ φ → ψ` for every formula `ψ` satisfied by `v`. -/
def IsAtomic (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → M), ∃ φ : L.Formula (Fin n), φ.Realize v ∧
    ∀ ψ : L.Formula (Fin n), ψ.Realize v → T ⊨ᵇ (φ ⟹ ψ)

/-- Atomicity is invariant under isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem IsAtomic.of_equiv {M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T} (hM : IsAtomic M) (e : M ≃[L] N) :
    IsAtomic N := by
  intro n v
  obtain ⟨φ, hφ, hψ⟩ := hM n (e.symm ∘ v)
  have hv : v = e ∘ (e.symm ∘ v) := by
    ext i
    simp
  refine ⟨φ, ?_, fun ψ hψ' => hψ ψ ?_⟩
  · rw [hv, StrongHomClass.realize_formula]
    exact hφ
  · rw [hv, StrongHomClass.realize_formula] at hψ'
    exact hψ'

/-- The class of atomic models of `T` is *categorical in `κ`* if it contains exactly one model of
cardinality `κ` up to isomorphism: there is an atomic model of `T` of cardinality `κ`, and any two
atomic models of `T` of cardinality `κ` are isomorphic.

Since the class of atomic models is not an elementary class, the Löwenheim–Skolem theorems do not
provide models of every infinite cardinality, so existence is part of the definition. -/
def AtomicCategorical (κ : Cardinal.{w}) (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomic M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomic M → IsAtomic N → #M = κ → #N = κ →
      Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/-- If the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`, then `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem AtomicCategorical.exists_isAtomic {κ : Cardinal.{w}} (h : AtomicCategorical κ T) :
    ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomic M ∧ #M = κ :=
  h.1

/-- **Shelah's categoricity problem for atomic classes.**
Let `T` be a complete first order theory in a countable language. If the class of atomic models
of `T` is categorical in `ℵ_n` for every `n < ω`, is it categorical in every infinite cardinal?

Here "categorical in `κ`" means that the class has exactly one model of cardinality `κ` up to
isomorphism. The conclusion is stated for all infinite cardinals `κ`; the case `κ = ℵ₀` is
harmless, since a complete theory has at most one countable atomic model up to isomorphism. -/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem categorical :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory), Countable L.Symbols →
      T.IsComplete → (∀ n : ℕ, AtomicCategorical.{u, v, w} (ℵ_ n) T) →
        ∀ κ : Cardinal.{w}, ℵ₀ ≤ κ → AtomicCategorical κ T := by
  sorry

end Categorical

/-!
# Categoricity of the class of atomic models

Shelah's problem: if the class of atomic models of a complete first-order theory (in a countable
language) is categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every $n < \omega$, is it categorical in every
infinite cardinal?

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Categorical theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

  of $\psi \in L_{\omega_1,\omega}$. Parts A and B*, Israel J. Math. 46 (1983), 212–240 and 241–273.
- J. T. Baldwin, *Categoricity*, University Lecture Series 50, American Mathematical Society (2009).
-/

namespace Categorical

open FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language Cardinal

universe u v w

variable {L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}} (T : L.Theory)

/-- A model `M` of `T` is *atomic* if every finite tuple `a` of elements of `M` realizes an
isolated (principal) complete type: there is a formula `φ` with `M ⊨ φ(a)` such that every
formula `ψ` with `M ⊨ ψ(a)` satisfies `T ⊨ ∀ x, (φ(x) → ψ(x))`. -/
def IsAtomicModel (M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → M), ∃ φ : L.Formula (Fin n),
    φ.Realize a ∧ ∀ ψ : L.Formula (Fin n), ψ.Realize a → φ ⟹[T] ψ

/-- The class of atomic models of `T` is *categorical in `κ`* if `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ` and any two atomic models of `T` of cardinality `κ` are isomorphic.
(Existence is part of the definition: the class of atomic models is not an elementary class, so the
Löwenheim–Skolem theorems do not provide models of every infinite cardinality.) -/
def AtomicModelsCategorical (κ : Cardinal.{w}) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M → IsAtomicModel T N →
      #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/-- If the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`, then `T` has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem AtomicModelsCategorical.exists_isAtomicModel {κ : Cardinal.{w}}
    (h : AtomicModelsCategorical T κ) :
    ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ :=
  h.1

/-- If `T` is `κ`-categorical (in the sense of `Cardinal.Categorical`) and has an atomic model of
cardinality `κ`, then the class of atomic models of `T` is categorical in `κ`. -/
@[category API, AMS 3]
theorem AtomicModelsCategorical.of_categorical {κ : Cardinal.{w}} (h : κ.Categorical T)
    (h' : ∃ M : Theory.ModelType.{u, v, w} T, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ) :
    AtomicModelsCategorical T κ :=
  ⟨h', fun M N _ _ hM hN => h M N hM hN⟩

**Shelah's problem on atomic classes.** Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory in a countable
language. If the class of atomic models of $T$ is categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every
$n < \omega$, is it categorical in every infinite cardinal?

Here "categorical in $\lambda$" means that $T$ has an atomic model of cardinality $\lambda$ and
that all atomic models of $T$ of cardinality $\lambda$ are isomorphic. Since the countable atomic
model of $T$ is unique when it exists, this is the same as asking for categoricity in every
uncountable cardinal.

Shelah proved a positive answer under the set-theoretic assumption
$2^{\aleph_n} < 2^{\aleph_{n+1}}$ for all $n < \omega$; the question in ZFC is open.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem categorical :
    answer(sorry) ↔
      ∀ (L : FirstOrder.Language.{u, v}) (T : L.Theory), Countable L.Symbols → T.IsComplete →
        (∀ n : ℕ, AtomicModelsCategorical T (ℵ_ n : Cardinal.{w})) →
          ∀ κ : Cardinal.{w}, ℵ₀ ≤ κ → AtomicModelsCategorical T κ := by
  sorry

end Categorical

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Categoricity of atomic models

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Categorical theory*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace Categorical

open Cardinal FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

/-- A model of `T` is atomic if the complete type of every finite tuple is isolated. -/
def IsAtomicModel {L : FirstOrder.Language} (T : L.Theory) (M : T.ModelType) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (v : Fin n → M), ∃ φ : L.Formula (Fin n),
    Formula.equivSentence φ ∈ T.typeOf v ∧
      ∀ p : T.CompleteType (Fin n), Formula.equivSentence φ ∈ p → p = T.typeOf v

/-- The atomic models of `T` are categorical in `κ` if an atomic model of size `κ` exists
and any two atomic models of size `κ` are isomorphic. -/
def IsAtomicCategorical {L : FirstOrder.Language} (T : L.Theory) (κ : Cardinal) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : T.ModelType, IsAtomicModel T M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : T.ModelType, IsAtomicModel T M → IsAtomicModel T N →
      #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/--
If the class of atomic models of a complete first-order theory in a countable language is
categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every $n < \omega$, is it categorical in every infinite cardinal?
Here categoricity includes the existence of an atomic model of the specified cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem categorical :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ {L : FirstOrder.Language}, Countable L.Symbols →
      ∀ {T : L.Theory}, T.IsComplete →
        (∀ n : ℕ, IsAtomicCategorical T (Cardinal.aleph n)) →
          ∀ κ : Cardinal, Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ κ → IsAtomicCategorical T κ := by
  sorry

end Categorical
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “the ℵ_n” as every aleph indexed by n : ℕ, as specified by the decomposition.
Restricted the language to be countable using `Countable L.Symbols`, following Mathlib and the nearby Vaught conjecture formalization.
Interpreted “every cardinal” as every infinite cardinal, expressed by `Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ κ`.

Defined an atomic model by requiring the complete type over the empty set of every finite tuple to be isolated by a formula: the formula belongs to that tuple's type and to no other complete type over the theory.

Defined categoricity of the class of atomic models to include existence at the specified cardinal as well as pairwise isomorphism of all atomic models of that cardinal, because Mathlib's `Cardinal.Categorical` only expresses the latter and is vacuously true when no such model exists.
Used Mathlib's bundled `Theory.ModelType`, whose carriers are nonempty models of the theory, and its language isomorphism `≃[L]`.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: `Cardinal.Categorical` quantifies over all models of a theory and only requires any two models of the target size to be isomorphic; it neither restricts to atomic models nor requires one to exist.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Categoricity of atomic models

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, *Categorical theory*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Categorical_%28model_theory%29)
- [Wikipedia, *List of unsolved problems in mathematics*](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace Categorical

open Cardinal FirstOrder FirstOrder.Language

/-- A model is atomic if the complete type of every finite tuple is isolated. -/
def IsAtomicModel {L : Language} {T : L.Theory} (M : T.ModelType) : Prop :=
  ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : Fin n → M), IsOpen ({T.typeOf a} : Set (T.CompleteType (Fin n)))

/-- The atomic models of `T` are categorical in `κ` if one exists in that cardinality and
any two such models are isomorphic. -/
def AtomicCategorical {L : Language} (κ : Cardinal) (T : L.Theory) : Prop :=
  (∃ M : T.ModelType, IsAtomicModel M ∧ #M = κ) ∧
    ∀ M N : T.ModelType, IsAtomicModel M → IsAtomicModel N →
      #M = κ → #N = κ → Nonempty (M ≃[L] N)

/--
Let $T$ be a complete first-order theory in a countable language. If the class of atomic
models of $T$ is categorical in $\aleph_n$ for every $n < \omega$, is it categorical in
every infinite cardinal? Here categoricity includes the existence of an atomic model of the
given cardinality.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3]
theorem categorical :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (L : Language) (_ : Countable L.Symbols) (T : L.Theory),
      T.IsComplete →
      (∀ n : ℕ, AtomicCategorical (aleph n) T) →
      ∀ κ : Cardinal, ℵ₀ ≤ κ → AtomicCategorical κ T := by
  sorry

end Categorical
modeling_decisions: Interpreted “categorical in the ℵ_n” as categoricity in `Cardinal.aleph n` for every `n : ℕ`, including `n = 0`, as specified by the decomposition notes.
Made the implicit countable-language hypothesis explicit as `Countable L.Symbols`.
Interpreted “every cardinal” as every infinite cardinal, encoded by `Cardinal.aleph0 ≤ κ`.

Defined an atomic model by requiring the complete type over the empty parameter set of every finite tuple `Fin n → M` to be an isolated point of Mathlib's Stone space of complete types; isolation is encoded by openness of the singleton.
Required categoricity of the atomic subclass in a cardinal to include both existence of an atomic model of that cardinality and uniqueness up to first-order language isomorphism.
Used `answer(sorry) ↔ ...` because the source is an open yes/no question.

new_definitions.why_needed: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have complete types and their Stone topology, but no predicate for atomic first-order models.

new_definitions.closest_existing_considered: `Cardinal.Categorical` compares all models of a theory and does not restrict to atomic models or require existence, so using it would be both too broad and potentially vacuous.
new_definitions.name: Categorical.AtomicCategorical
new_definitions.why_needed: The conjecture concerns categoricity of the non-elementary subclass of atomic models and explicitly requires existence at the given cardinality.
